meaning: The number 34 has no prominent or well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
description: Unlike numbers such as 7, 12, 40 or 18, which have deep symbolic roots in the Bible and Jewish tradition, 34 is not a number attributed with special mystical or theological significance. It does not appear as a prominent symbolic number in the Torah, Talmud or Kabbalistic numerology. In the Bible, the number is mentioned, among other places, in Genesis 11:16, where Eber was thirty-four years old when he fathered his son Peleg, but this is a genealogical detail without added symbolic value. Some modern numerological interpretations may attempt to assign it meaning by combining the numbers 3 and 4, but this has no basis in classical biblical or rabbinic tradition.

footnotes.text: The name Peleg is linked to the Hebrew verb פלג (palag), which means "to divide". According to Genesis 10:25, he was given this name because "in his days the earth was divided". However, the fact that Eber was 34 years old when Peleg was born is not attributed any symbolic meaning in rabbinic literature.
